answer:
Let $X\in\mathbb R^{N\times d_{in}}$, $W\in\mathbb R^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}$, $b\in\mathbb R^{d_{out}}$, and $Y=XW^T+\mathbf1b^T$. Given $G\in\mathbb R^{N\times d_{out}}$, the differential is $dY=dXW^T+XdW^T+\mathbf1db^T$. Substituting into $dL=\operatorname{tr}(G^TdY)$ and collecting coefficients yields the backward pass. [1](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/)

$$\nabla_XL=GW,\qquad\nabla_WL=G^TX,\qquad\nabla_bL=G^T\mathbf1.$$

The shapes are respectively $N\times d_{in}$, $d_{out}\times d_{in}$, and $d_{out}$. For extra leading dimensions such as batch and sequence, flatten those dimensions for parameter-gradient accumulation, then restore the input shape. Broadcasting the bias requires summing every broadcast axis. An upstream gradient already reflecting a mean loss must not be divided by the batch size again.
